rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says Moses feared the people would disperse after seeing the magic before he could demonstrate the staff; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it as contrary to the verse's sequence and God's reassurance.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه خاف أن يتفرق الناس بعد رؤية سحرهم ولا يصبروا إلى أن يلقي عصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' inward fear shows that the magicians' display seemed to resemble or approach his miracle, although their magic was unreal and his sign had real substance; God calls their magic great.
rows.anchor: يظهر من إيجاسه عليه السلام خيفة في نفسه أنهم أظهروا للناس من السحر ما يشابه آيته المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command not to fear is meant to strengthen and support Moses: because he is superior to them in every respect, their trick cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: نهي بداعي التقوية والتأييد وقد علله بقوله { انك أنت الأعلى } فالمعنى انك فوقهم من كل جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the staff what is in Moses' right hand points to the lack of intrinsic reality in things: by God's will it can be a staff or a living serpent.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه إشارة إلى أن ليس للشيء من الحقيقة إلا ما أراد الله فإن أراد لما في اليمين أن يكون عصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the magicians' serpents what they made frames the contest as God's unrestricted power against human fabrication, which is false and vanishing before God's word.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن المغالبة واقعة بين تلك القدرة المطلقة التي تتبعها الأشياء في أساميها وحقائقها وبين هذا الصنع البشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff's swallowing displays Moses' superiority to the senses, while the verse's conclusion displays his superiority in reality because falsehood has no reality and truth need not fear it.
rows.anchor: بيان لكونه عليه السلام أعلى بحسب ظاهر الحس كما أن في ذيله بيانا لكونه أعلى بحسب الحقيقة إذ لا حقيقة للباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of their work as a sorcerer's trick explains its being swallowed and shows why Moses' miracle prevails: their magic lacks reality while his sign has it.
rows.anchor: لأن ما معهم كيد ساحر لا حقيقة له وما معه آية معجزة ذات حقيقة والحق يعلو ولا يعلى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sorcerer gains only an illusion for observers, so an unreal undertaking cannot yield genuine success or happiness; this is the major premise behind the claim that sorcerers do not prosper.
rows.anchor: فإن الذي يناله الساحر بسحره خيال من الناظرين باطل لا حقيقة له ولا فلاح ولا سعادة حقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that sorcerers do not prosper resembles statements that God does not guide wrongdoers and derives from the principle that falsehood vanishes and God effaces it while establishing truth.
rows.anchor: والجميع من فروع إن الباطل كان زهوقا الإسراء 81، ويمح الله الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsehood keeps embellishing itself as truth, but truth eventually erases it; Moses' staff swallowing the magic illustrates a pattern applying to every falsehood and the truth that destroys it.
rows.anchor: فلا يزال الباطل يزين أمورا ويشبهها بالحق ولا يزال الحق يمحوه ويلقف ما أظهره لوهم الناظرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording that the magicians were made to fall prostrate, instead of saying they prostrated, depicts divine power subduing and overwhelming them until they had no choice.
rows.anchor: بالبناء للمفعول دون أن يقال فسجد السحرة إشاره إلى إذلال القدرة الإلهية لهم وغشيان الحق بظهوره إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confession names the Lord through both Moses and Aaron, thereby testifying both to God's lordship and to the two prophets' messengership.
rows.anchor: ليكون فيه الشهادة على ربوبيته تعالى ورسالة موسى وهارون معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase they said is uncoordinated because it answers an implied question about what the magicians said.
rows.anchor: من غير عطف لكونه كالجواب لسؤال مقدر كأنه قيل فما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting hands and feet crosswise means cutting the right hand and left foot; crucifixion is intensified or multiplied, and the trunks are palm trunks.
rows.anchor: وقطع الأيدي والأرجل من خلاف أن يقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى والتصليب تكثير الصلب وتشديده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's question about their believing before permission may be an interrogative with an omitted particle expressing denial, or a declarative sentence meant to establish their alleged crime.
rows.anchor: والجملة استفهامية محذوفة الأداة والاستفهام للإنكار أو خبرية مسوقة لتقرير الجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of a political pact with Moses to stage his prophecy, gather Egyptians and the magicians, then feign defeat so the crowd follows and the established order is removed.
rows.anchor: كأنهم تواطؤوا مع رئيسهم أن يتنبأ موسى فيدعو أهل مصر إلى الله ويأتي في ذلك بسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh repeats the charge elsewhere as a plot in the city to expel its people; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the accusation was meant to incite the public against the magicians, as Pharaoh had incited them against Moses earlier.
rows.anchor: إنما رماهم بهذا القول تهييجا للعامة عليهم كما رمى موسى عليه السلام بمثله في أول يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an records Pharaoh's threat of severe punishment but does not state whether he actually carried it out.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر تعالى في كلامه أنجز فيهم ذلك أم لا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians' answer is rhetorically powerful, conveying profound wisdom and certainty in its wording, implications, and meaning.
rows.anchor: كلام بليغ في منطوقه بالغ في مفهومه بعيد في معناه رفيع في منزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians had been awed by Pharaoh and worldly finery, even proclaiming victory by his might; after seeing truth's signs, they lost their awe of his power and worldly status and were freed from cowardice, flattery, caprice, and longing for worldly glitter.
rows.anchor: فما لبثوا دون أن ظهرت لهم آيات الحق فبهرت أبصارهم فطاحت عند ذلك ما كانوا يرون لفرعون من عزة وسلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers now attach themselves to truth and God's authority: they will what God wills, hope only in God, and fear only God.
rows.anchor: فلا يريدون إلا ما أراده الله ولا يرجون إلا الله ولا يخافون إلا الله عز اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is oblivious to God, sees only himself as Egypt's lord with subjects, land, and armies, and imagines truth must submit to his falsehood and people's recognition of truth must await his permission.
rows.anchor: يرى أن الحق تبع باطله والحقيقة خاضعة مطيعة لدعواه فيتوقع أن لا تمس نفوس الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh treats the physical body and its decay as the only human reality and material pleasures as the only happiness, as shown by his threat of bodily torture.
rows.anchor: ويرى أن لا حقيقة للإنسان إلا هذه البنية الجسمانية التي تعيش ثم تفسد وتفنى وأن لا سعادة له إلا نيل هذه اللذائذ المادية الفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers regard Pharaoh's worldly wealth and status as a deceptive mirage; they face a choice between truth and falsehood, and people of certainty cannot prefer the mirage over truth.
rows.anchor: فقد خيروا بين الحق، والباطل والحقيقة والسراب، وحاشا أهل اليقين أن يشكوا في يقينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying they will not prefer Pharaoh, the magicians mean they will not prefer the broad worldly resources and gains he claimed to own, rather than merely his person.
rows.anchor: فليس مرادهم به إيثار شخص بما هو جسد إنساني ذو روح بل ما معه مما كان يدعيه أنه يملكه من الدنيا العريضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This closing section of Moses' story counts God's favors to Israel, especially rescue, the Mount appointment, and manna and quail; it leads into the calf story and centers on Israel's exposure to God's anger.
rows.anchor: يعد سبحانه فيه جملا من مننه على بني إسرائيل كإنجائهم من عدوهم ومواعدتهم جانب الطور الأيمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to Israel has an implied introductory We said, and their enemy is Pharaoh, whom God drowned after their long ordeal while saving them.
rows.anchor: كأن الكلام بتقدير القول أي قلنا يا بني إسرائيل وقوله { قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم } المراد به فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointment at the right side of the Mount likely means Moses' forty-night appointment to receive the Torah; the stories of the manna and quail have also appeared in al-Baqara and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد بهذه المواعدة مواعدة موسى أربعين ليلة لإنزال التوراة وقد مرت القصة في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to eat the good provisions is permissive in force; the phrase good things of what We provided is an adjective joined to its noun, since God's provision is not divided into good and non-good, as another verse confirms.
rows.anchor: إباحة في صورة الأمر وإضافه الطيبات إلى { ما رزقناكم } من إضافة الصفه إلى الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgression in consuming the provision means ingratitude and failure to give thanks, illustrated by Israel's complaint about having only one food.
rows.anchor: وذلك بكفران النعمة وعدم أداء شكره كما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's anger becoming due is expressed by a verb also used of a debt becoming payable; divine anger is an active attribute realized by willing harm through causes arranged after a servant's disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي يجب غضبي ويلزم من حل الدين يحل من باب ضرب إذا وجب أداؤه والغضب من صفاته تعالى الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one upon whom God's anger settles has fallen, from the word for falling, and this is interpreted as destruction.
rows.anchor: أي سقط من الهوي بمعنى السقوط وفسر بالهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic promise of mercy follows the severe warning; the intensive form of very forgiving signals abundant forgiveness rather than simply saying I forgive or I will forgive.
rows.anchor: وعد بالرحمة المؤكدة عقيب الوعيد الشديد ولذا وصف نفسه بكثرة المغفرة فقال { وإني لغفار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance can mean turning from sin to obedience or from associating partners to monotheism; faith can mean belief in God, His signs and messengers, or the rulings they brought, and the verse's broad wording includes both kinds.
rows.anchor: والتوبة وهي الرجوع كما تكون عن المعصية إلى الطاعة كذلك تكون من الشرك إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Israel committed both sins and shirk through calf worship, the verse need not be restricted; its open wording includes all repentant believers, since divine attributes such as forgiveness are not limited to one people.
rows.anchor: فلا موجب لصرف الكلام عن ظاهر إطلاقه في التوبة عن الشرك والمعصية جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's abundant forgiveness reaches anyone who repents from shirk or sin, believes in God or His revealed signs and laws, regrets wrongdoing, and replaces disobedience with obedience; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers to his earlier treatment of repentance.
rows.anchor: وإني لكثير المغفرة لكل إنسان تاب وآمن سواء تاب عن شرك أو عن معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is the opposite of misguidance, as shown in two other verses; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī asks whether then guided means not returning to the same sin, not straying in other actions, or both.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله { ثم اهتدى } فالاهتداء يقابل الضلال كما يشهد به قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because then indicates sequence, its apparent sense is steadfastness in repentance, equivalent to the requirement of reform elsewhere; however, this reading raises difficulties about the intensive forgiveness for one repented sin and treating disobedience as disbelief.
rows.anchor: ظاهر العطف بثم أن يكون المراد هو المعنى الأول فيفيد معنى الثبات والاستقامة على التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible reading takes repentance and faith as turning from shirk and believing in God, with righteous action as obedience to His commands; then repeated lapses create many occasions for abundant forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فيمكن أن يقال إن المراد بالتوبة والإيمان التوبة من الشرك والإيمان بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forgiveness of sins parallels the promise in another verse, while then guided adds that the believer must follow the way and approach through its proper door.
rows.anchor: فقوله { وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا } ينطبق على آية النساء ويبقى فيه شرط زائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The only scriptural condition on acceptance of faith and good works is faith in the Messenger through submission and obedience in all matters, receiving religion from him, and following his path without independent innovation; this is his authority over believers in religion and worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: ولا نجد في كلامه تعالى ما يقيد الإيمان بالله والعمل الصالح في تأثيره وقبوله عند الله إلا الإيمان بالرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance intended by the verse is following the Messenger in religion and worldly affairs, that is, entering under his authority; Israel's hesitation about Moses' and Aaron's authority explains why the condition follows the warning against transgression.
rows.anchor: فقد تبين أن المراد بالاهتداء في الآية على ما يهدي إليه سائر الآيات هو الإيمان بالرسول باتباعه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes then guided to mean remaining steadfast in faith throughout one's life.
rows.anchor: فقد قيل الاهتداء لزوم الإيمان والاستمرار عليه ما دامت الحياة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says guidance means not doubting one's faith again.
rows.anchor: وقيل أن لا يشك ثانيا في إيمانه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies guidance with following the Prophet's Sunnah and avoiding innovation.
rows.anchor: وقيل { الأخذ بسنة النبي وعدم سلوك سبيل البدعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says guidance is knowing that one's deeds will be rewarded.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاهتداء هو أن يعلم أن لعمله ثوابا يجزى عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says guidance is cleansing the heart of blameworthy traits.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو تطهير القلب من الأخلاق الذميمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation defines guidance as guarding belief from contradiction with the truth in any matter; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says none of these views has evidence and the term should mean something distinct from faith and righteous action.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو حفظ العقيدة من أن تخالف الحق في شيء فإن الاهتداء بهذا الوجه غير الإيمان وغير العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue took place at the Mount appointment when Moses received the Torah, as recounted in detail elsewhere; the question asks why he arrived ahead of his people, apparently expected to come together.
rows.anchor: حكاية مكالمة وقعت بينه تعالى وبين موسى عليه السلام في ميعاد الطور الذي نزلت عليه فيه التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says his people are following closely and will arrive soon; he hurried ahead to win God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: أي إنهم لسائرون على أثري وسيلحقون بي عن قريب { وعجلت إليك رب لترضى } أي والسبب في عجلي هو أن احصل رضاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people following Moses were the seventy men he chose for the appointment, not all Israel; Aaron's being left in charge and the later question about the delay support this reading.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالقوم وقد ذكر أنهم على أثره هم السبعون رجلا الذين اختارهم لميقات ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question to Moses could have come at the beginning or end of the appointment; since the calf inquiry was not about an already existing calf during the journey, the report that the test followed impatience at Moses' absence allows the sequence to stand without strained explanations.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخطاب يمكن أن يخاطب به موسى عليه السلام في بدء حضوره في ميعاد الطور كما يمكن أن يخاطب في أواخر عهده به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna means testing, and the Samiri is credited with misleading Israel because he fashioned the calf that they then worshipped, making him an operative cause of their error.
rows.anchor: الفتنة الامتحان والاختبار ونسبة الإضلال إلى السامري - وهو الذي سبك العجل وأخرجه لهم فعبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal particle in God's reply corrects the reassurance implied by Moses' report that the people are following him: their apparent good state should not be trusted because they were tested and went astray.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله { فإنا قد فتنا قومك } للتعليل يعلل به ما يفهم من سابق الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase your people may refer to the whole population here, unlike its earlier reference to the seventy men Moses selected for the appointment.
rows.anchor: وقوله { قومك } من وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر ولعل المراد غير المراد به في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angry describes intense anger, while asafan can mean grief or intense anger; breaking Moses' promise means failing to maintain the people well while he was away, as another verse confirms.
rows.anchor: الغضبان صفة مشبهة من الغضب، وكذا الأسف من الأسف بفتحتين وهو الحزن وشدة الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks whether his absence lasted so long that the people despaired of his return and their order fell apart.
rows.anchor: وهو مدة مفارقة موسى إياهم حتى يكونوا آيسين من رجوعه فيختل النظم بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good promise may mean the Torah and the happiness that following God's law brings in both worlds, or God's rescue of Israel, establishment in the land, and abundant favors.
rows.anchor: وهو أن ينزل عليهم التوراة فيها حكم الله وفي الأخذ بها سعادة دنياهم وأخراهم - أو وعده تعالى أن ينجيهم من عدوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' question about inviting God's anger means they transgressed by returning to disbelief after faith and worshipping the calf.
rows.anchor: فطغوتم بالكفر به بعد الإيمان وعبدتم العجل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported explanation says Israel broke its promise by not following Moses when he ordered them to join him.
rows.anchor: كقول بعضهم إن إخلافهم موعده أنه أمرهم أن يلحقوا به فتركوا المسير على أثره

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says Moses had ordered Israel to obey Aaron until he returned, but they disobeyed.
rows.anchor: وقول بعضهم هو أنه أمرهم بطاعة هارون بعده إلى أن يرجع إليهم فخالفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wilayah in the cited report means authority over people's religious and worldly affairs: reference for religious knowledge and law and for managing society.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالولاية في الحديث ولاية أمر الناس في دينهم ودنياهم وهي المرجعية في أخذ معارف الدين وشرائعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had this authority by the verse saying he is closer to believers than themselves; after him it belongs to his family through the verse of wilayah and widely transmitted reports including Thaqalayn and Manzila.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما ينص عليه الكتاب في أمثال قوله { النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse appears among addresses to Israel, it is not confined to them: Moses had this authority over his community, and the verse guides people in the Prophet's era to his authority and thereafter to the Imams of his family.
rows.anchor: والآية وإن وقعت بين آيات خوطب بها بنو إسرائيل وظاهرها ذلك لكنها غير مقيدة بشيء يخصها بهم

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi objects that interpreting guidance as the authority of the Prophet's family in an address to Israel would mean God informed Moses' people of that duty, which he says no sound report establishes; he accepts their love and its obligation.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن ولايتهم وحبهم رضي الله عنهم مما لا كلام عندنا في وجوبه لكن حمل الاهتداء في الآية على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi's objection rests on treating wilayah as love and restricting the verse to Israel; the author says wilayah means governance and control that entail following and obedience, while love is an extended, secondary sense supported by the kinship-love evidence.
rows.anchor: وليست الولاية في آياتها وأخبارها بمعنى المحبة وإنما هي ملك التدبير والتصرف في الأمور الذي من شؤونه لزوم الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wilayah can also mean God's own guardianship of a servant: God manages and directs the affairs of the sincerely devoted; its attribution to the Prophet's family is figurative because they pioneered this path.
rows.anchor: ولولاية أهل البيت عليهم السلام معنى آخر ثالث وهو أن يلي الله أمر عبده فيكون هو المدبر لأموره والمتصرف في شؤونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is attributed primarily to God and by extension to those He favored, including prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous.
rows.anchor: كما ينسب الصراط المستقيم في كلامه تعالى إليه بالأصالة وإلى الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين
